items.title: JJ Johnson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: So Clark Monroe hired me to play nightly, just until Coleman Hawkins got there.

ctx.x: It was a religion with him, so much so that Coleman Hawkins would be in the White Rose, I believe was the name of this bar, which was right around the corner from the Three Deuces. He would stay there at the bar having a beer or such until such time as he felt he should go on the stand and play. That may be a half an hour after the starting time. It could be as late as an hour after the starting time or as brief as ten minutes after
the starting time. But to start on time was against his principles. He just did not do so. So Clark Monroe hired me to play nightly, just until Coleman Hawkins got there.
